picks.title: AI music can be difficult to detect, but there are some telltale signs
picks.excerpt: Engadget's guide to spotting AI-generated tracks: what to listen for in vocals, lyrics and instrumentals, plus quick ways to check whether an artist is real.
picks.rationale: A practical checklist listeners and curators can use right away to spot AI tracks (vocals, lyrics, instrumentals, artist footprint). Earlier cards covered detector tools, not how to listen for the signs.

picks.title: Weakening AI copyright law will spell 'disaster for creativity', global music body warns Albanese
picks.excerpt: Exclusive: IFPI's chief tells Australia's government that opening online content to AI training would be a 'huge mistake' that damages the country's reputation.
picks.rationale: The global recording-industry body is lobbying directly against an AI training exception in Australia. If the exception passes, it changes whether music can be used to train AI there without a licence.

picks.title: 조영수 오래된 노래, 버추얼 가수 '원'의 숨으로 피어나다 [인터뷰]
picks.excerpt: Hitmaker composer Cho Young-soo launches his first AI virtual artist WON, debuting Nov 8 with single 'Mama Song'; he says 'if AI scores 99, the last 1% is the human's part' and targets the Billboard chart.
picks.rationale: A new launch: a mainstream K-pop hitmaker debuts his own AI virtual singer and explains how he splits the work between AI and human songwriters.

picks.title: The new Ivors Composer Awards is pushing back against AI
picks.excerpt: With AI threatening composers' rights and livelihoods, the Ivors Academy's new Composer Awards aims to raise the profile of human screen and media composers.
picks.rationale: A concrete institutional move: the Ivors Academy has launched an awards format built to spotlight human screen and media composers as AI pressure grows. Earlier cards only had commentary on this.

picks.title: How Close to the Theme? Similarity-Label Conditioning for Game Music Generation
picks.excerpt: Fine-tunes a pretrained MIDI model on Super Mario section pairs so composers can dial how similar newly generated sections are to a theme, from near-repeat to new material.
picks.rationale: A controllable-generation method that lets a composer set how closely new material should follow a theme, from near-repeat to new material. That is a practical setting for game and adaptive scoring, and it differs from earlier symbolic-control papers (MuLaCover, MI-MIDI 2), which steer key or tone rather than similarity to a theme.

dedup.note: RE-PICK: removed arXiv 2611.07210 'Latent Terrain' because the orchestrator found it is the same tool (the Latent Terrain Max/MSP package) that music already published on 2026-06-30 (https://cdm.link/latent-terrain-max/). A paper about an already-covered tool is not a new action. Replaced it with arXiv 2611.01047, game-music similarity-label conditioning.
